title: Affine radicial preparation with geometrically reduced generic fibre before generic-flat shrinking
statement: Let $X$ be affine and $f:X\to T$ locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $V\subseteq T$ be an affine open containing the image of $f$, and let $\eta$ be a generic point of $T$ such that the fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. There exist an affine open $U\subseteq T$ containing $\eta$, an integral affine scheme $S$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], a reduced affine scheme $Y$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], a universal homeomorphism $q:S\to U$ [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism], and a locally finite type morphism $g:Y\to S$. There is a generic point $\eta\prime$ of $S$ mapping to $\eta$, the fibre $Y_{\eta\prime}$ is geometrically reduced (its extension to every field extension of the residue field is reduced), and for every $s\in S$ the fibre $Y_s$ is geometrically irreducible if and only if $X_{q(s)}$ is geometrically irreducible. Here $q(s)$ is regarded as a point of $T$. No flatness or finite presentation is asserted for $g$.

source.place: Tag 0559, second proof, reductions and finite purely inseparable extension before the final generic-flat shrinking; Tags 051T and 052A.

proof.text: Nonemptiness of the generic fibre puts the generic point in the given affine open. Factor through that open and reduce both schemes. The reduced irreducible base is integral, reduction maps are universal homeomorphisms, and geometric fibre irreducibility is preserved.

Apply generic flat finite presentation to the reduced finite type affine family. Shrink to a principal open to retain both affineness properties. The reduced flat source ring embeds in its generic fibre, which is a domain because the fibre is geometrically irreducible.

Let K be the base fraction field and L the generic source function field. Choose a finite purely inseparable extension K prime such that the reduction of L tensor K prime is separably generated. Scale each field generator b satisfying b to the q equals a/d to db, whose q-th power is a times d to the q minus one. Adjoin these scaled generators to the base ring. The finite integral radicial domain has fraction field K prime and its spectrum is a universal homeomorphism.

Base change the source to this finite radicial affine base and reduce it. Its generic fibre embeds in the separably generated function field, which remains reduced under all field extensions; hence the generic fibre is geometrically reduced. The source is affine, reduced and locally of finite type. Reduction and purely inseparable base change preserve geometric fibre spaces and therefore geometric irreducibility at every point, including empty fibres. The base homeomorphism lifts the generic point uniquely. Do not make a second generic-flat shrinking here.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_radicial_generic_reduced_preparation
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (V : T.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (himage : Set.range f ⊆ V)
    (η : T) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ)
    (hgeom : GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField η)) :
    ∃ (U : T.Opens), η ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧
      ∃ (S Y : Scheme.{u}) (q : S ⟶ U.toScheme) (g : Y ⟶ S),
        IsAffine S ∧ IsIntegral S ∧ IsAffine Y ∧ IsReduced Y ∧
        IsUniversalHomeomorphism q ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧
        ∃ η' : S, IsGenericPoint η' Set.univ ∧ (q ≫ U.ι) η' = η ∧
          GeometricallyReduced (g.fiberToSpecResidueField η') ∧
          ∀ s : S, GeometricallyIrreducible (g.fiberToSpecResidueField s) ↔
            GeometricallyIrreducible (f.fiberToSpecResidueField ((q ≫ U.ι) s))
